title: Impact of Analyst Buy Recommendations on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model.
- Why: We observe returns in event time around a single, well-defined information shock (the analyst buy recommendation). Event studies identify the immediate causal impact by comparing abnormal returns on the event day to a modeled counterfactual based on normal return dynamics.
- Implementation: For each stock i, estimate a stock-specific alpha_i from pre-event days and use the provided beta_i to form abnormal returns AR_it = ret_it − (alpha_i + beta_i × mkt_ret_it). The 1-day CAR is AR on event day 0. We test whether the cross-sectional average 1-day CAR is negative.
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding concurrent news on average at event day (exogeneity of event timing, or at least zero-mean confounding across the cross-section).
  - Correct model for normal returns (market model with provided beta_i and estimated alpha_i is adequate over the short window).
  - No anticipation or leakage that would systematically shift day −1 or earlier returns (checked via regression robustness using day −1 as baseline).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# 0) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s58_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic sanity
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))
df <- df[order(df$stock_id, df$event_day), ]
df$stock_id <- as.integer(df$stock_id)
df$event_day <- as.integer(df$event_day)

# 1) Compute abnormal returns (market model with provided beta_i and estimated alpha_i)
#    Estimate alpha_i using pre-event window (default: event_day <= -6; fallback: event_day < 0)
df$excess_mkt <- df$ret - df$beta * df$mkt_ret

# Primary alpha: use event_day <= -6
pre_mask1 <- df$event_day <= -6
alphas1 <- tapply(df$excess_mkt[pre_mask1], df$stock_id[pre_mask1],
                  function(x) if (length(x) > 0) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)

# Fallback alpha: use all pre-event days (< 0)
pre_mask2 <- df$event_day < 0
alphas2 <- tapply(df$excess_mkt[pre_mask2], df$stock_id[pre_mask2],
                  function(x) if (length(x) > 0) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)

# Map alphas back to all rows
df$alpha_hat <- alphas1[as.character(df$stock_id)]
na_idx <- is.na(df$alpha_hat)
df$alpha_hat[na_idx] <- alphas2[as.character(df$stock_id[na_idx])]
df$alpha_hat[is.na(df$alpha_hat)] <- 0  # final fallback if a stock has no pre-event data

# Abnormal return (AR)
df$ar_mm <- df$ret - (df$alpha_hat + df$beta * df$mkt_ret)

# 2) Main result: 1-day CAR on event day 0 (equals AR on day 0)
d0 <- df[df$event_day == 0, ]
if (nrow(d0) == 0) stop("No event_day == 0 rows found. Cannot compute 1-day CAR.")

car0 <- d0$ar_mm
N0 <- length(car0)
mean_car0 <- mean(car0, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_car0 <- sd(car0, na.rm = TRUE)
se_car0 <- sd_car0 / sqrt(N0)
t_car0 <- if (se_car0 > 0) mean_car0 / se_car0 else NA_real_
p_car0 <- if (is.na(t_car0)) NA_real_ else 2 * pt(abs(t_car0), df = N0 - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("Main result (market model):\n")
cat("Mean 1-day CAR [day 0] =", sprintf("%.4f", mean_car0),
    "(", sprintf("%.2f", mean_car0*100), "% )\n", sep = " ")
cat("t-stat =", sprintf("%.3f", t_car0),
    " p-value =", format(p_car0, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    " N =", N0, "\n\n")

# 3) Robustness A: Market-adjusted returns (MAR = ret - mkt_ret) at day 0
d0$mar <- d0$ret - d0$mkt_ret
mean_mar0 <- mean(d0$mar, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_mar0 <- sd(d0$mar, na.rm = TRUE)
se_mar0 <- sd_mar0 / sqrt(N0)
t_mar0 <- if (se_mar0 > 0) mean_mar0 / se_mar0 else NA_real_
p_mar0 <- if (is.na(t_mar0)) NA_real_ else 2 * pt(abs(t_mar0), df = N0 - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("Robustness A (market-adjusted):\n")
cat("Mean 1-day CAR [day 0] =", sprintf("%.4f", mean_mar0),
    "(", sprintf("%.2f", mean_mar0*100), "% )\n", sep = " ")
cat("t-stat =", sprintf("%.3f", t_mar0),
    " p-value =", format(p_mar0, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    " N =", N0, "\n\n")

# 4) Robustness B: Alternative alpha window (use all pre-event days <= -1)
alphas_alt <- tapply(df$excess_mkt[df$event_day <= -1], df$stock_id[df$event_day <= -1],
                     function(x) if (length(x) > 0) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)
d0$alpha_alt <- alphas_alt[as.character(d0$stock_id)]
d0$alpha_alt[is.na(d0$alpha_alt)] <- 0
d0$ar_mm_alt <- d0$ret - (d0$alpha_alt + d0$beta * d0$mkt_ret)

mean_car0_alt <- mean(d0$ar_mm_alt, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_car0_alt <- sd(d0$ar_mm_alt, na.rm = TRUE)
se_car0_alt <- sd_car0_alt / sqrt(N0)
t_car0_alt <- if (se_car0_alt > 0) mean_car0_alt / se_car0_alt else NA_real_
p_car0_alt <- if (is.na(t_car0_alt)) NA_real_ else 2 * pt(abs(t_car0_alt), df = N0 - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("Robustness B (alternative alpha window <= -1):\n")
cat("Mean 1-day CAR [day 0] =", sprintf("%.4f", mean_car0_alt),
    "(", sprintf("%.2f", mean_car0_alt*100), "% )\n", sep = " ")
cat("t-stat =", sprintf("%.3f", t_car0_alt),
    " p-value =", format(p_car0_alt, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    " N =", N0, "\n\n")

# 5) Robustness C: Two-day CAR [0, +1] using market model ARs (require both days present)
has0 <- tapply(df$event_day == 0, df$stock_id, function(x) any(x, na.rm = TRUE))
has1 <- tapply(df$event_day == 1, df$stock_id, function(x) any(x, na.rm = TRUE))
valid_ids <- intersect(names(which(has0)), names(which(has1)))
valid_ids <- intersect(valid_ids, unique(as.character(df$stock_id)))

car01 <- numeric(0)
if (length(valid_ids) > 0) {
  for (sid in valid_ids) {
    sid_i <- as.integer(sid)
    rows <- df$stock_id == sid_i & df$event_day %in% c(0, 1)
    car01 <- c(car01, sum(df$ar_mm[rows], na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  N01 <- length(car01)
  mean_car01 <- mean(car01, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_car01 <- sd(car01, na.rm = TRUE)
  se_car01 <- sd_car01 / sqrt(N01)
  t_car01 <- if (se_car01 > 0) mean_car01 / se_car01 else NA_real_
  p_car01 <- if (is.na(t_car01)) NA_real_ else 2 * pt(abs(t_car01), df = N01 - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

  cat("Robustness C (two-day CAR [0,+1], market model):\n")
  cat("Mean CAR[0,+1] =", sprintf("%.4f", mean_car01),
      "(", sprintf("%.2f", mean_car01*100), "% )\n", sep = " ")
  cat("t-stat =", sprintf("%.3f", t_car01),
      " p-value =", format(p_car01, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
      " N =", N01, "\n\n")
} else {
  cat("Robustness C: No stocks have both day 0 and day +1 observations; skipping CAR[0,+1].\n\n")
}

# 6) Robustness D: Regression-based event-time estimate (day 0 vs pre-event day -1)
#    Residualize market via provided betas: y = ret - beta*mkt_ret
df$y_resid <- df$ret - df$beta * df$mkt_ret

if (any(df$event_day < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  # Choose reference pre-event day: prefer -1; otherwise the max available negative day
  if (any(df$event_day == -1)) {
    ref_day <- -1L
  } else {
    ref_day <- max(df$event_day[df$event_day < 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  df$event_day_fac <- factor(df$event_day)
  # Relevel event_day with chosen reference
  df$event_day_fac <- relevel(df$event_day_fac, ref = as.character(ref_day))
  # Fit regression: y ~ stock FE + event-day FE
  reg_formula <- as.formula("y_resid ~ factor(stock_id) + event_day_fac")
  fit <- lm(reg_formula, data = df)
  # Extract coefficient for event_day 0 (relative to day ref_day)
  coefs <- coef(summary(fit))
  coef_name <- paste0("event_day_fac", 0L)
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    gamma0 <- coefs[coef_name, "Estimate"]
    se_gamma0 <- coefs[coef_name, "Std. Error"]
    t_gamma0 <- coefs[coef_name, "t value"]
    p_gamma0 <- coefs[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"]
    cat("Robustness D (regression-based event study, day 0 vs day", ref_day, "):\n")
    cat("Estimated abnormal return (gamma_0) =", sprintf("%.4f", gamma0),
        "(", sprintf("%.2f", gamma0*100), "% )\n", sep = " ")
    cat("t-stat =", sprintf("%.3f", t_gamma0),
        " p-value =", format(p_gamma0, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n\n")
  } else {
    cat("Robustness D: day 0 coefficient not estimable (possibly missing day 0 in regression).\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Robustness D: No negative pre-event days available; skipping regression-based check.\n\n")
}

# Final reminder of main estimate for clarity
cat("Summary: Mean 1-day CAR [day 0, market model] =",
    sprintf("%.4f", mean_car0), " (", sprintf("%.2f", mean_car0*100), "% ),",
    " t =", sprintf("%.3f", t_car0),
    " p =", format(p_car0, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    " N =", N0, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Buy recommendations typically convey favorable private/processed information, leading to an immediate upward price reaction.
- Magnitude: Approximately +0.3% to +1.0% average 1-day CAR (day 0), with stronger effects if recommendations are surprises or from influential analysts. Two-day CAR [0,+1] may be slightly larger (e.g., +0.5% to +1.5%).
- Interpretation: A significantly negative 1-day CAR would be counter to prior literature and would suggest either confounding news, sample-specific effects, or that “buy” recommendations in this dataset follow prior run-ups and elicit contrarian responses.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare 1-day CAR before and after the recommendation event.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests a negative impact of analyst buy recommendations on 1-day CAR.
